fields.meta_title: Job Application Form Template and Builder | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Make a job application form that takes resumes and keeps every applicant in a database you own. Print a PDF of any application. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Job Application Form That Feeds Your Hiring Pipeline
fields.hero_description: Describe the role and what each applicant must provide. Emergent builds the job application form and its applicant database, and you own both the data and the code.
fields.features_heading: What Every Job Application Form Needs
fields.features_subheading: A job application form puts the same questions to every candidate for a role. Emergent builds the form and the record it feeds.
fields.feature_1:
Every section, field by field

Emergent drafts the six standard sections: applicant information, position and availability, work history, education, references, and certification. Each field gets a proper input.
fields.feature_2:
One form for every open role

Applicants pick a position and see only the questions written for it. A nurse is asked for a license number and expiry date; a designer is asked for a portfolio and a salary range.
fields.feature_3:
Resume and license uploads

Applicants attach a resume and any license the role needs from a phone, without creating an account. Each file is stored with the application it arrived on, beside the answers.
fields.feature_4:
A PDF copy of any application

Ask for PDF copies and the app lays out each application like the paper form you use today, ready for the personnel file. Nobody retypes an online answer to get a paper copy.
fields.feature_5:
An applicant table with hiring stages

Every application lands as a row with role, location, stage, and owner, in a table that never caps submissions. The app then alerts the hiring manager by Slack or email.
fields.feature_6:
Your careers page, your source code

Publish the form on your own domain or embed it in the careers page you already run. Engineering can extend the hiring flow from the full source, exported to your GitHub.

fields.usecase_heading: Job Application Forms for Every Hire
fields.tab_content_1:
An hourly job application that leads with availability

The first question is which store. Applicants then tap the shifts they can work on a weekly grid and give a start date. That store's manager hears about it in Slack, and a filter on the table shows at a glance who can cover weekends.
fields.tab_content_2:
A clinical job application that checks the license

Each nurse or medical assistant gives a license number and the state that issued it. The expiry date has its own field, and any license due to lapse within 60 days is flagged for the recruiter before an interview is booked. Certifications such as BLS upload on the same screen.
fields.tab_content_3:
An internal application that loops in the manager

Employees apply with their employee ID and their months in the current role. Anyone short of the posting's minimum tenure is told before they submit. Eligible applications alert the person's current manager and go to a table kept apart from outside candidates.
fields.tab_content_4:
A professional application that sorts by must-haves

Designers and other salaried candidates upload a resume with a portfolio, then answer two must-have questions on work authorization and salary range. Missing either one sends the application to a hold list. Everyone else goes to the hiring manager as a Slack shortlist.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Job Application Form
fields.howto_description: Start from the usual sections, then add what each role needs. Seven steps take you from a list of requirements to a published form that fills an applicant table.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Write down what the role requires
fields.howto_step_1_des: List what you need to know before a first call: availability, location, licenses, the right to work, and pay expectations. A question that would not change the decision stays off the form. Applicants on a phone will finish a short form on a break; a long one waits for later.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Name the sections you want, or ask for the standard set. Work history repeats for every past job the applicant lists, and references repeat the same way. The form closes with a certification the applicant signs and dates: I certify that my answers are true and complete.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Give each position its own questions in the prompt. A delivery role might ask about a driver's license and recent violations, while a cashier role skips them. Applicants see only the questions for the role they pick, and the shared sections read the same for everyone.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Add an upload field for the resume and a second one for any certificate the role calls for, then mark which ones are required. A cover letter can stay optional for hourly roles and required for office ones.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Choose who hears about each application and how: the store manager in Slack, the recruiter by email. Then name the stages every applicant moves through before an offer. With a stage column added, the applicant table becomes the hiring pipeline your managers filter each morning.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Keep a PDF copy for records
fields.howto_step_6_des: Decide what happens on paper. HR may want a filled PDF of each application for its records, and walk-in applicants need a way in. A QR code at the counter opens the same form on a phone; a few blank printed copies cover anyone without one.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Put the form on your careers page or your own domain, then submit a test application for every role. Check that each role shows its own questions and that the alert reaches the right person before the link goes out.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Job Application Form That Feeds Your Hiring Pipeline', title 'Job Application Form Template and Builder | Emergent' and hero 'Emergent builds the job application form and its applicant database' cover the whole job, not one feature or a sibling topic (defect 1 clear).

intent.evidence: Cycle-1 fix holds: FAQ 3 lays out the form field by field ('Work history, per job: employer, title, dates, supervisor, reason for leaving, permission to contact'), howto_step_2 gives the certification text, and FAQ 8 and FAQ 11 cover the blank printable PDF the top 10 (rocklinusd, circuit7, Iowa, DS-1950 PDFs) serve. No AMBER angle needed (Builder-fit); F5 accepted.

specificity.evidence: Hiring variant in the table ('Prompt for the application form and the hiring pipeline around it'); buyer vocabulary throughout: 'reasons for leaving and permission to contact references', 'any license due to lapse within 60 days is flagged for the recruiter before an interview is booked', 'months in the current role', 'a driver's license and recent violations' (defect 3 clear).

openers.evidence: Every paragraph opens on a full sentence: feature_1 'Emergent drafts the six standard sections...', tab_content_1 'The first question is which store.', howto_step_6 'Decide what happens on paper.'; no keyword labels (defect 2 clear).

craft.evidence: Cycle-2 fix holds: zero ', so' and zero ', which' tails on the page; sentences end on their point ('...flagged for the recruiter before an interview is booked.', 'Anything else waits for the interview.'); longest FAQ sentence well under 32 words; no 'and not before'-style trailers (defects 4, 6 clear).

voice.evidence: Cycle-2 fix holds: tab openings now differ in shape ('The first question is which store.' / 'Each nurse or medical assistant gives...' / 'Employees apply with...' / 'Designers and other salaried candidates upload...'); the role-example triplet is split (nurse/designer in feature_2, delivery/cashier in howto_step_3); 'six standard sections' appears once, 'one record, not an inbox' is gone; lines like 'Applicants on a phone will finish a short form on a break; a long one waits for later.' read human.

truth.evidence: PDF story is now one rule: FAQ 11 'The blank PDF has as many rows as you ask for: request one past job and one reference, and Emergent lays it out on a single letter page', consistent with FAQ 8 'blank PDF, sized for letter paper', FAQ 9 'the most recent job and one reference', FAQ 5 'printable version for walk-ins' and feature_4 'A PDF copy of any application'; 'instead of three' is gone; meta 'Print a PDF of any application' matches feature_4. FAQ 4, 13, 14 describe built-app behaviour ('the app can save...', 'the app can send a short decline') within the capability principle; the typed signature carries no legal-validity claim. Table facts from the library (V2/V3 clean); claims_used all approved.

distinct.evidence: Shift grid by store, clinical license-expiry flag, internal tenure check and must-have hold list are specific to hiring; new-employee-form, candidate-screening-form and creator-application are linked, not overlapped ('Payroll and emergency contact details come after the offer'); no sibling primary in a heading; D2 clean.

faq.evidence: 15 items, each answered in its first sentence ('Yes, if each section asks for less.', 'Usually not.'); cycle-2 repeats fixed with new information: FAQ 13 'set a size limit, for example 10 MB per file... refused at upload with a message', FAQ 14 'a confirmation email right away... a short decline', FAQ 4 'Haddad_RN.pdf'; FAQ 10 now answers use ('to decide whom to interview and hire'); FAQ 3 list is useful by design; links help ('new employee form', 'candidate screening form'); no contradictions between FAQ 4, 8, 9, 11.
